bib.title: Algorithms for Hyper-Parameter Optimization
bib.venue: not printed in the PDF text (no venue line on page 1)

question: Can sequential model-based optimisation (GP and TPE with expected improvement) find better DBN hyper-parameters than random search and manual search in a tree-structured space?
hypothesis: Algorithmic sequential search outperforms both manual and random search when many trials are affordable.
contributions: Random search is competitive with the manual optimization of DBNs in [1]
Automatic sequential optimization outperforms both manual and random search
Two novel techniques for response-surface models with irrelevant elements: hierarchical GP and tree-structured Parzen estimator

method.summary: Compares random search, grid-assisted manual search (Larochelle 2007), a hierarchical GP-EI SMBO and TPE (EI via l(x)/g(x)) on a 32-variable DBN search space for the convex and MRBI datasets, up to 200 trials each, parallelised over 5 GPUs.
method.task: hyper-parameter optimisation of deep belief networks (classification)

limits: Only DBNs on two datasets; no repeats of the 200-trial runs stated, so no variance across searches.
Authors concede SMBO can be arbitrarily bad with a poor p(y|x), or slower than random if it finds a local optimum.
Reasons TPE beat GP are untested hypotheses.
Search spaces differ from manual search (larger, no discretisation); TPE could leave initial bounds while GP and random could not.

terms.definition: models p(x|y) as l(x) if y < y*, g(x) if y >= y*, with l from observations with loss below y* and g from the rest; y* is the gamma quantile of observed y, so p(y<y*)=gamma
EI_y*(x) proportional to (gamma + g(x)/l(x) (1-gamma))^-1: pick x with high l(x) and low g(x); draw candidates from l and rank by g(x)/l(x)
EI_y*(x) := integral of max(y*-y,0) p_M(y|x) dy
